problem: OlmoEarth attends over the whole observation window; a materialized cache goes stale as new acquisitions arrive. Can a small source-trained update module, given only the previous cache state and the single-acquisition embeddings of the new images, approximate the full-window re-encoding closely enough to keep downstream maps as good as re-encoding, at a fraction of encoder cost?

novelty_claim_boundary.claimed: streaming approximation of a full-window EO foundation-model representation with a learned state update, evaluated on downstream labels and measured encoder cost; the predicted-vs-observed residual gate is ours
not_claimed: change-timing detection (Sen12 has one terminal mask)
compute savings of the initial encode

development: Sen12 folds holdout_chimanimani and holdout_hiroshima (both exposed); train = 600-tile subsample of train regions, val = fold val region, test = fold test region; T=12, cutoffs (4,6,8,10,12), step = 2 new acquisitions

metrics.agreement: cosine and relative MSE vs teacher at c=12
metrics.downstream_primary: exact AP of the FROZEN mean-cache decoder (p4_native_control seed1) applied to the student state vs applied to the teacher
metrics.cost: encoded timestep-units: 36 (re-encode each step) vs 12 (streaming, incl. initial 4)

screen_rule.pass: residual module recovers >= 90% of the teacher's downstream AP gap over frozen m_4 in BOTH folds (seed mean) AND beats gru and ema by >= .01 AP in both folds
screen_rule.partial: gru or ema also recovers >= 90%: 'streaming is easy'; report utility, no method claim
screen_rule.fail: no module recovers >= 70% in either fold: full re-encode stays necessary on this task; close T1 on Sen12

next_if_pass: external tasks with per-timestep tensors and DATED labels (KuroSiwo 3-date floods, SEN12 monthly urban, GLO annual lakes): add delay/false-alarm curves; freeze confirmatory criteria first
gpu: extraction ~1 h for ~3,000 tiles (52 timestep-units/tile), 18 runs ~2 h; runs alongside the 4-arm on GPU1 (own processes only)
